verdicts.why: MCU Wiki: in Inhumans ep 4-5 Locus is captured by Black Bolt and Medusa, kept in Louise's trunk, still says she believes in Maximus, and is shot; her only affiliation is the Attilan Royal Guard. Capture and death are not moves, so the Independent stage and left title go.

The Army order is wrong, but the Army is not a stage at all: Marko was a WWI soldier about 15 years before the series, shown only in flashback (S1E5), and was already Silvermane's man when the series starts. Under the owner's rule that is backstory, so drop it rather than move it. Silvermane's Mob then Independent (S1E8, Silvermane killed) stays.

The move to Fury's side happens off screen (MCU Wiki cites the Captain Marvel Prelude comic), and Infinity War only shows her next to Fury in the post-credits scene. 'Nick Fury's Crew' is a wiki label that neither the dataset nor the films use as a group. An unsure case keeps what's there.

The return does happen in S3, not Slingshot: MCU Wiki says she demands to leave and walks out of the Playground in 'The Team' (AoS317), then comes back in 'Emancipation' (AoS320). But walking out is a quit, so an Independent stage belongs between them; the proposal drops it. Her left list should also get 'Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3'.

MCU Wiki: in WandaVision ep 6, Hayward has Darcy, Woo and Rambeau ordered off the Response Base (removed from the operation, which counts as fired). After they break back in, she hacks Hayward's files against him and never works for S.W.O.R.D. again. Independent plus left at WandaVision is right.

MCU Wiki ('Retirement'): after the Chronicom war in AoS713 'What We're Fighting For', Fitz and Simmons retire from S.H.I.E.L.D. to raise Alya, and Daisy calls him retired at the reunion. That is a real departure, so left gets S7. The matching Independent S7 stage is handled in a separate item.

Same person as Fitz, and this file carries the S7 step: he retires from S.H.I.E.L.D. with Simmons in AoS713 (MCU Wiki 'Retirement'). Adding 'Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S7' to left is right, and the existing S4 entry stays.

MCU Wiki: Daredevil frees her from Red Hook (S2E3), and at Ariana's safehouse the fugitives record testimony for the resistance (S2E4), where the Swordsman is the one who 'chose to not join the resistance'. The wiki lists her among its members. The dataset's name for this group is "Matt's resistance", not "Daredevil's Army". With two stages, '(from the start)' becomes her first title.
MCU Wiki: K'un-Lun is centuries-old backstory (he was banished and co-founded the Hand), and his affiliation is the Hand through Iron Fist S1 and The Defenders. There is no move to K'un-Lun and back.

MCU Wiki: after Terrigenesis Gordon brings her to Afterlife (AoS211-212). She accepts 'my life here... to help my people', works as Afterlife's fortune teller, and stays there until Jiaying kills her (AoS221). Her S2 work for Whitehall was forced by a control device. Afterlife is the dataset's group name, as in Lincoln's record.

Marvel Database: at the end of Across the Spider-Verse, Gwen puts together a splinter group to work against the Spider Society, Peter and Mayday among them. Spider Society is listed as a former affiliation. This matches Gwen's record (Spider-Society, then Independent, with a left).

Marvel Database files the cartoon's Charles Cameo as Reality = Earth-6799, the reality of the 1967 series. Its Earth-67 page calls Earth-67 'a divergent version of Earth-6799' from the comics. Note: the Spider-Man 1967 cameos in the Spider-Verse films are filed as Earth-67, so a blanket change to all 33 records needs a per-record check.
Marvel Database: Master Technician has Reality = Earth-6799, first appearing in the 1967 series S2 ep 3. Earth-6799 is 'the reality where the 1967 Spider-Man animated series takes place'.

MCU Wiki: in What If...? S1E9 the Guardians go home, and the Watcher puts Natasha in the world that lost its Widow. She stops Loki, and Fury offers her a place in that world's new Avengers. Marvel Database gives the Avengers of Earth-51825 as her current affiliation and the Guardians as former.

The X-Factor stage is wrong: Marvel Database's X-Factor (Earth-92131) roster leaves her out, and Wikipedia's S2E2 summary only has her leading X-Force into X-Factor's trap. But a left at S2 has no departure behind it. Genosha fell in S1, and the dataset keeps Genosha for other survivors (Moira, Banshee). Marvel Database still lists the Inner Circle as her current group. Drop X-Factor and keep left empty.

MCU Wiki (History Altered by Chronicoms): Malick recruits trainee Garrett in 'Stolen' (AoS710). In 'The End is at Hand' (AoS712, ep 135), after Malick leaves him to die, he 'decided to turn his back on Malick and rejoin S.H.I.E.L.D.' and teleports Coulson, May and Yo-Yo out before Hand shoots him. The infobox lists both groups.

Marvel Database ('Joining the X-Men'): Forge and Storm join the X-Men at Xavier's call in X-Men '97 S1E9, and Forge is put on Gold Team against Bastion. In S1E10 he runs the roster at the mansion. The stage belongs to S1.

Marvel Database and MCU Wiki: in Eyes of Wakanda ep 4 Prince Tafari is on his first War Dogs mission with Kuda and returns to Wakanda with him. Both list the War Dogs as his current affiliation, and nothing on screen takes him out. The closing 'Wakanda' stage has no move behind it.

Marvel Database files two characters. Flint (Earth-17516), from S5, stays in 2091 to rebuild Earth. Flint (Earth-199999), from S6E11, is 'a duplicate... created by Elena Rodriguez and Alphonso Mackenzie through the Di'Allas of Creation' and lists no affiliation. Splitting at episode 122 is right.

Carina is the Collector's slave and servant (MCU Wiki: 'former slave'; category Tivan Group Employees). That is servitude in a workplace, not a tracked group, and the dataset never uses 'The Tivan Group'. Freeing herself from a captor is not a move. The proposal also uses 'What If...?' where the record's form is 'What If...? S1'.

MCU Wiki: Laura (Agent 19) retired from S.H.I.E.L.D. before any title she's on file for, and Fury kept her out of the files and set up the farm. Hawkeye only reveals that past through her watch. Under the owner's rule S.H.I.E.L.D. is backstory, and neither left title has a departure.

The sources disagree. MCU Wiki gives her no affiliation (she is the court's advisor and lists the Avengers only as allies), while Marvel Database lists the Avengers. A court post is a workplace role, and restraining Thor to help Carter's band is not clearly joining it. Her twin case, Sir Nicholas Fury, is also Independent. An unsure case keeps what's there.

Testament Industries is the Schultzes' company (MCU Wiki: Anderson was its co-leader). The dataset doesn't track it as a group, and the owner's rule says workplaces like this are rejected while that question is decided separately.

MCU Wiki: Murakami's K'un-Lun training and banishment, when he co-founded the Hand, are centuries-old backstory. In The Defenders, his only title, his affiliation is the Hand, so the one Hand stage from the start is right.
